# Conversational Customer Service: A Detailed Guide


October 7, 2026 • 13 MIN READ


Authors


Gayathri Vishwanthan is a freelance B2B writer specialising in customer success and customer service. Her work for the Sprinklr blog helps readers understand and act on the metrics that matter, from customer success KPIs and retention strategies to conversational customer service. She has a clear talent for turning a data-heavy subject like customer retention or success measurement into a structured, practical guide that teams can genuinely use.

Aishwarya Suresh is an experienced content writer specializing in social media management, social listening, social analytics, Voice of the Customer (VoC) and customer experience. She writes practical, research-backed guides that help brands understand customer conversations, measure social media performance and turn insights into meaningful business decisions.


[View full bio](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/author/aishwarya-suresh/)


**Key Takeaways:**


- Conversational customer service combines AI, automation, and human support to resolve customer issues through natural, context-aware conversations.
- Unlike traditional support models, conversational service maintains context across voice, messaging, social media, email, and self-service channels.
- AI agents and agent copilots can automate routine requests, assist agents in real time, and improve resolution speed without sacrificing personalization.
- The biggest benefits include improved customer satisfaction, lower service costs, stronger agent productivity, and reduced customer churn.
- Successful conversational customer service strategies balance automation with human empathy while continuously improving through analytics and customer feedback.


Conversational customer service is a way of supporting customers through natural, two-way conversations on the channels they already use, such as chat, messaging apps, social media, email, and voice. AI agents handle routine requests instantly. Human agents take the complex ones, and they start with the full context of the conversation.


You've probably been the customer in this story. You explain a billing issue to a chatbot, get transferred to an agent, and then explain it all over again. The technology worked. The conversation broke somewhere in between.


That gap is getting expensive to ignore. McKinsey reports that[35%](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/operations/our-insights/operations-blog/agentic-ai-in-customer-care-whats-on-leaders-minds) of organizations plan to automate more than 60% of inbound inquiries by 2028. Customers are drawing a line of their own, though:[87%](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-08-04-gartner-survey-finds-87-percent-of-customers-say-companies-using-genai-for-customer-service-must-provide-access-to-a-human-agent0) say companies using generative AI must still give them access to a human. The brands getting this right use AI for speed and people for judgment, and they keep one continuous conversation connecting both.


This guide covers how conversational customer service works, the benefits it delivers, practical ways to improve it, and a step-by-step plan to implement it.


Table of Contents


- What is conversational customer service?
- Benefits of conversational customer service
- Tips to improve conversational customer service
- Final thoughts


##


What is conversational customer service?


Conversational customer service is a strategy focused on establishing customer connections through natural conversations. Technologies like artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML) and generative AI are deployed to understand customer intent and provide responses that mimic human conversations.


You can use AI agents,[chatbots](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/what-is-a-chatbot/) and voice-based technologies to hold conversations with customers. Human agents step in whenever a situation calls for empathy or judgment.


As more customers expect brands to go beyond transactional relationships, conversational customer service helps improve[customer engagement](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/customer-engagement/) and retention.


Let's look at how it benefits brands and customers, and what brands can do to implement it. First, here's why moving away from traditional customer service matters.


### Traditional vs. conversational customer service


Traditional customer service is typically rigid. Agents follow pre-written scripts or workflows, which can limit how personal or empathetic they can be. Conversational customer service uses technologies like AI to create natural, engaging interactions between customers and businesses. Take a look at the following example.


Here are the other ways conversational customer service outperforms the traditional model:


**Feature**


**Traditional Customer Service**


**Conversational Customer Service**


**Communication Style**


Often formal and scripted


Natural, conversational, and personalized


**Channels**


Primarily phone, email, in-person


Omnichannel: chat, social media, messaging apps, voice and email in one thread


**Response Time**


May involve wait times and delayed responses


Real-time or near-real-time interactions, 24/7


**Customer Interaction**


One-way communication from business to customer


Interactive, two-way communication


**Context Retention**


Customers repeat details at every handoff


Conversation history carries across channels and agents


**Personalization**


Limited personalization


Highly personalized based on customer data


**Automation**


Limited automation with basic IVR systems


AI agents that complete tasks end to end, plus conversational IVR


**Agent Support**


Manual search across multiple tools


AI copilots that summarize, suggest replies and surface knowledge


**Proactive Engagement**


Reactive - responds to customer inquiries


Proactive - initiates conversations and offers support


**Customer Experience**


May vary in consistency and quality


Consistently focused on enhancing customer experience


**Scalability**


May face challenges scaling with growing customer demands


Easily scalable, adapts to varying workloads


***Is conversational customer service the same as omnichannel customer service?*** **


They're related but not the same. Omnichannel customer service connects all your support channels so customers can switch between them. Conversational customer service describes how the interaction feels on those channels: natural, two-way, and aware of context. The best programs combine both, so a customer can start on WhatsApp, move to a phone call, and keep one continuous conversation.


##


Benefits of conversational customer service


Customers expect prompt and efficient service. Conversational customer service can help you meet these expectations by providing customers with immediate access to information and support. It can automate repetitive tasks and aid customer service agents in being responsive and delivering a smooth experience to customers.


It can also help you with the following:


### 1. Improved customer service


Conversational customer service is a more convenient and engaging way of delivering[customer service](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/what-is-customer-service/) .


It allows customers to engage with your agents using their preferred[customer service channels](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/customer-service-channels/) , such as chat, messaging, or social media. They can interact with your agents or chatbots in their own time without having to wait on hold or navigate complex phone menus.


More importantly, AI-powered conversational tools help your agents understand customer preferences and tailor support. For example, they can remember a customer's past interactions and suggest relevant information or recommendations. That personal touch pays off. McKinsey finds that businesses leading in customer experience outperform peers on growth and total shareholder returns, often by as much as[two times](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/growth-marketing-and-sales/our-insights/rewiring-customer-experience-for-the-agentic-era) .


### 2. Reduced costs


AI agents now do much more than answer FAQs. They can complete tasks such as processing refunds, rescheduling appointments, and updating accounts. Gartner predicts that by 2029, agentic AI will autonomously resolve[80%](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-03-05-gartner-predicts-agentic-ai-will-autonomously-resolve-80-percent-of-common-customer-service-issues-without-human-intervention-by-20290) of common customer service issues without human intervention, leading to a 30% reduction in operational costs.


Conversational customer service can reduce costs for brands in several ways:


- **Lower cost per interaction:** AI agents resolve high-volume, repetitive requests end to end, so human agents can focus on complex cases.
- **Reduced training costs:** AI copilots surface the right knowledge during live conversations, which shortens ramp-up time for new agents.
- **Increased customer satisfaction:** Faster, more accurate resolutions reduce repeat contacts and escalations, which lowers service costs over time.


***Also Read:*** **[How to Use Conversational AI for Customer Service](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/conversational-ai-for-customer-service/)


### 3. Shorter response time


Every minute a customer spends proving who they are or waiting on hold adds friction. Conversational customer service removes much of it. In McKinsey's research,[62%](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/operations/our-insights/operations-blog/agentic-ai-in-customer-care-whats-on-leaders-minds) of customer care leaders expect authentication and call summaries to eventually be fully automated. This is where conversational customer service helps. AI agents and virtual assistants give customers immediate support at any hour and resolve many questions without a human. When a person is needed, the handoff comes with context, so the customer doesn't have to start over.


***Learn more:***[Tips on Improving Customer Response Time with AI](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/improve-customer-service-response-time-with-AI/)


### 4. Improved agent efficiency


Customer service agents often get boggled by the sheer volume of customer queries. It leaves them with little time to focus on high-value tasks, such as building relationships with customers and providing personalized support. It also takes a toll on their efficiency.


Conversational customer service moves routine work to[self-service](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/customer-self-service/) and AI agents. For example, you can give customers access to a[knowledge base](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/knowledge-base/) and let AI agents handle simple transactions. Service leaders expect AI agents to cut service costs and case resolution times by[20%](https://www.salesforce.com/ap/blog/state-of-service/) on average.


For the conversations agents do handle, AI copilots summarize the case, pull answers from knowledge articles and suggest next steps in real time. According to Salesforce, service reps using AI spend[20%](https://www.salesforceben.com/salesforce-says-ai-will-handle-50-of-customer-service-cases-by-2027-are-they-right/) less time on routine cases, which frees up about four hours a week for complex work.


Options like[customer service automation](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/customer-service-automation/) and self-service can reduce the volume of queries and help agents manage their tasks more efficiently.


### 5. Reduced customer churn


Customer churn is a major concern for brands, regardless of their size.


- Customers may switch to a competitor if they're unhappy with your service, which can significantly hurt revenue.
- Several factors can contribute to customer churn, including poor customer service, lack of personalization, and lack of engagement.
- Poor customer service is a major factor that drives customers away. Long wait times, unhelpful or rude agents, and unresolved issues can make customers feel undervalued and dissatisfied.


Conversational customer service can solve this problem. It can help your agents provide personalized responses to customer queries by using customer data to tailor responses to their individual needs. For instance, an agent could use a customer's purchase history to recommend products or services they are likely interested in.


AI agents and virtual assistants also keep conversations going between human touchpoints, which improves the overall experience.


Use conversational service to stop customers from leaving.


***Also Read:***[7 Proven Ways to Reduce Customer Churn Rate](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/how-to-reduce-customer-churn/)


***What are some examples of conversational customer service?***


Common examples include a customer tracking an order and changing the delivery address in one WhatsApp chat, or a bank's voice assistant resolving a card block over the phone. Another is an airline's AI agent rebooking a disrupted flight and then passing a refund dispute to a human agent with the full history attached. In each case, the customer talks naturally and the brand keeps the context.


##


Tips to improve conversational customer service


Implementing conversational customer service is only the start. You need to keep improving it, so it delivers the results you expect. That includes tracking metrics, using the right tools, analyzing customer sentiment, and refining conversations.


Here's how you can improve the quality of conversational customer service:


### Use AI tools to be more responsive


Today's conversational tools go well beyond scripted chatbots. AI agents understand intent, handle several questions in one conversation, and take actions like scheduling callbacks or updating orders. That improves response time and personalizes each interaction.


Use these tools to understand customer needs, spot patterns, and find opportunities to cross-sell and upsell. Service professionals expect agentic AI to lift upsell revenue by[15%](https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/state-of-service-report-announcement-2025/) .


Take the example of[Aramex](https://www.sprinklr.com/newsroom/aramex-selects-sprinklr-ai-chatbots-for-transformative-global-customer/) . The Dubai-based logistics and transportation solutions provider uses AI to automate chat conversations and serve customers quickly and efficiently.


Tools like these simplify your agents' work and transform the customer experience.


💡 **Pro Tip:**[Sprinklr AI Agents](https://www.sprinklr.com/products/platform/ai-agents/) resolve requests across voice, chat, email and social, and hand off to human agents with the full conversation history. For agents,[Sprinklr Copilot](https://www.sprinklr.com/products/platform/sprinklr-copilot/) sits inside the agent desktop. It summarizes cases, answers questions from knowledge articles and past cases, and recommends guided workflows during live conversations.


### Identify the metrics to measure


Every successful brand monitors a set of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to measure customer satisfaction. For example, metrics like customer satisfaction score (CSAT), net promoter score (NPS), and average handling time (AHT) help measure customer service efficiency.


Once AI agents are part of your service, track how well automation performs too. Useful measures include automated resolution rate, escalation rate, and the quality of handoffs to human agents.


® Identify the key customer service metrics that can help you improve customer service and measure them regularly.


***Not sure what metrics to measure? Start with these***[21 customer service metrics](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/customer-service-metrics/)


***What is the difference between conversational AI and conversational customer service?*** **


Conversational AI is the technology: the chatbots, voice bots and AI agents that understand and respond in natural language. Conversational customer service is the strategy that uses that technology together with human agents, customer data, and workflows to support customers. Put simply, conversational AI is one of the tools, and conversational customer service is the experience you build with it.


### Analyze conversations and make improvements


Tools like[conversation analytics](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/conversation-analytics/) use natural language processing (NLP) and ML to analyze customer interactions across email, chats, voice and social media.


Use them to understand customer sentiment and preferences and to personalize support. Modern tools also pick out the top reasons customers get in touch and recurring friction points automatically, so you can fix root causes instead of answering the same complaint over and over.


You can also use the insights gained to improve agent training and enhance the[quality of customer service](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/3-important-qualities-of-customer-service/) .


Brands like Telefônica Vivo use AI to analyze and route customer conversations on social channels and to suggest smart replies to agents. Automation handles the routine work, so agents can focus on complex cases. As a result, Vivo cut response times on social channels by 65%, and positive customer comments rose by 137%.


[Read full story](https://www.sprinklr.com/stories/vivo/)


### Train customer service agents to be more effective


While you rely on AI to improve customer interactions, keep investing in your customer service agents. Their role is growing: Gartner found that[85%](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-04-28-gartner-survey-finds-eighty-five-percent-of-service-and-support-leaders-are-expanding-human-agent-responsibilities-despite-expectations-of-mass-ai-layoffs) of service leaders are adding new responsibilities to frontline agent roles as AI takes over routine work.


Train agents on the new tools, introduce them to new workflows, and help them adapt to conversational customer service. This matters especially for tenured employees. Closing the skills gap improves both their skills and their performance.[84%](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-02-18-gartner-survey-finds-ninety-one-percent-of-customer-service-leaders-under-pressure-to-implement-ai-in-2026) of service leaders plan to add new skills to the agent role in 2026.


Monitor their progress and provide them with feedback and resources to improve their efficiency.


***Also Read:*** **[Using AI Scoring in Contact Centers to Tailor Agent Training Programs](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/use-ai-scoring-for-agent-training/)


### Keep the interaction humanized


Remember that the purpose of conversational customer service is to augment the role of human agents and not replace them.


Keep the interaction human. Customers are open to AI when they know a person is within reach.[87%](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-08-04-gartner-survey-finds-87-percent-of-customers-say-companies-using-genai-for-customer-service-must-provide-access-to-a-human-agent0) say companies using generative AI must preserve access to a human agent.


Encourage the customer service agents to keep the interaction conversational and free. Nudge them to use workflows to automate interactions but avoid using scripts while interacting with customers. This will help them understand the customer's problems better and solve them more efficiently.


***When should an AI agent hand a conversation over to a human?***


An AI agent should escalate when the customer asks for a person, when sentiment turns negative, when the issue involves money, security or a complaint, or when the AI isn't confident in its answer. A good handoff passes along the conversation history, customer details and steps already tried, so the human agent can continue without asking the customer to repeat anything.


### How to implement conversational customer service


We now know how conversational customer service can reduce churn, improve agents' efficiency, and save costs. Let's learn how to implement it in your company to boost customer engagement and retention.


#### Step 1: Align all key stakeholders


Conversational customer service is a new concept. Hence, you must align all key stakeholders and reach a consensus before implementing it. Speak to the operations and product teams, subject matter experts and customer service agents to identify[customer query scenarios](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/customer-service-scenarios/) . Discuss the best ways to manage such scenarios and train the agents and chatbots. This will help your agents to deliver superior customer experience.


#### Step 2: Choose the right tech stack


You cannot have conversations with customers without the help of the right tools and platforms. Choose ones that:


- Are easy to use
- Detect customer sentiment and respond with empathy
- Keep conversations and context consistent across channels
- Improve response speed
- Give agents a unified view of the customer and their history
- Support AI agents and AI copilots with built-in guardrails and human escalation


#### Step 3: Structure and label your data


If you use AI in conversational customer service, you need to structure your unstructured and semi-structured data. That lets you categorize and label it and train your AI models. Structured, labeled data helps AI understand it and respond to customer queries efficiently. Once the model is ready, integrate it into your workflow and get started. Unified data pays off: companies that unify their customer service channel data are[1.4x](https://www.salesforce.com/blog/state-of-service/) more likely to achieve a very successful AI implementation.


***Also Read:*** **[Customer Service Analytics – A Comprehensive Guide](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/customer-service-analytics/)


#### Step 4: Map your customer journeys


Customers rarely stay on one channel. They move between apps, websites, chat, and voice, and they expect the brand to keep up.[McKinsey](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/growth-marketing-and-sales/our-insights/rewiring-customer-experience-for-the-agentic-era) notes that many companies get limited results from AI because they layer it on top of fragmented journeys and let handoffs break context.


A[customer journey map](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/customer-journey-mapping/) will help you identify the possible touchpoints a customer could use to interact with the brand. This will help the agents understand the customer's journey and give them the context to serve the customers efficiently.


#### Step 5: Personalize customer communications


Customers get frustrated when the responses are not contextually relevant. It's important to understand the context and tailor the interactions accordingly. Use tools that help you understand the customer's profile, view previous transactions, and analyze the customer's sentiments. It will help you personalize the responses.


#### Step 6: Keep training your AI models


AI models and AI agents need continuous training to stay accurate, just like people. They can fall out of date if they aren't fine-tuned and maintained, so monitor them regularly. This helps you catch biases, integration issues, security risks, and inaccurate answers. Keep your knowledge base current, label new data and retrain models to improve accuracy and customer experience.


Getting this wrong carries real risk. Forrester predicts that[one-third](https://www.contentgrip.com/forrester-ai-predictions/) of companies will frustrate customers and erode trust in 2026 by rolling out generative AI self-service that isn't ready.


##


Final thoughts


Brands are realizing the significance of conversational customer service in retaining customers, reducing agent costs, and improving profits. If you are planning to transition from traditional to conversational customer service, remember to:


- Bring all stakeholders together to shortlist various customer service scenarios and train agents and AI models
- Choose the right tools like conversational AI and conversational IVR to automate customer service and make it more conversational
- Train agents to use these tools and adjust to new processes
- Structure and label data to train the machines
- Define and monitor KPIs regularly to improve customer satisfaction
- Train the AI models to ensure they are compliant and updated


All these steps will help you get started on the journey of adopting conversational customer service.
